messages:
oliver: Ran a quick nsys + perfetto on the stage cluster after the 2/16 deploy. TL;DR: small continuous-batch windows, but a recurring ~3-6ms tail on the kernel timeline after KV sweep passes. attaching traces: https://perfetto.local/trace/2245 and gs://redwood-traces/2245012345/nsys.tar.gz

maya: ugh, that tail is what we saw in prod yesterday during the 95p latency spike, right?

oliver: yes. produced on a p4d replica with quantized matmul kernels. sequence: request arrives -> batching window opens -> kvcache sweep triggered (hits ~70%) -> then kernel matmul executes but we see a secondary CUDA launch ~3-6ms later that stalls the host.

liam: can you paste the relevant perfetto slice? small snippets are easier to read than full trace.

oliver: sure — here's the kernel timeline excerpt from the perfetto UI: 
```
GPU Timeline (perfetto):
0.000ms  enqueue batch (host)
0.120ms  kvcache sweep start
0.280ms  kvcache sweep end  (KV hits 70%)
0.300ms  matmul_kernel<<<256,256>>>  elapsed 0.48ms
3.720ms  matmul_kernel<<<128,128>>>  launch overhead 4.1ms  <-- suspicious
7.850ms  host memcpy async
```

sophia: that secondary matmul looks like a fallback path — maybe kernel selection decided smaller grid and got enqueued later. do we have the kernel choice logs?

oliver: yes, runtime logs show: 
```
[2026-02-16T14:12:33.123Z] kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_fused_fp16_grid256
[2026-02-16T14:12:33.125Z] kvcache: sweep_start keys=48
[2026-02-16T14:12:33.129Z] kvcache: sweep_end hits=34 misses=14
[2026-02-16T14:12:33.130Z] kernel_selector: fallback=matmul_small_grid128 due_to=tail_latency_predictor
[2026-02-16T14:12:33.430Z] kernel_launch: matmul_small_grid128 queued
```

maya: so kernel_selector triggered a fallback because tail predictor estimated long remaining TTL? or because of batch fragmentation?

liam: My hunch: continuous-batching window is crowing small requests together but KVs cause slight variance in execution path. If sweep hits cleanup path, it shifts kernel selection to smaller grid to reduce memory pressure — but smaller grid has worse launch-to-exec ratio for this HW, so the effective overhead increases.

perf-bot: nsys summary attached: total GPU active 1.8ms, CPU->GPU queue wait 4.2ms, kernel-launch-latency mean 1.9ms, 95p launch-latency 4.9ms. Link: gs://redwood-traces/2245012345/nsys_summary.txt

sophia: exact. small-grid fallback increases launches and reduces occupancy; launch overhead becomes dominant. also note the host has a bunch of small memcpy tasks right after — could be KV serialization.

oliver: repro plan: 1) run controlled nsys on stage with injected KV miss rate (0%, 30%, 60%) 2) force kernel_selector to prefer large grid 3) measure 95p latency and CPU queue wait

maya: can you share the injection command?

oliver: using the local harness: 
```
# run harness with kv miss injection
./harness --profile nsys --kv-miss-rate 0.3 --batch-window 6ms --quant=fp16 --repeat 200
nsys profile --output ns-2245 ./target/bin/serve --config cfg.json
```

liam: add a flag to disable fallback for a controlled run: --kernel-force=grid256

oliver: will run now. quick note: when I forced grid256, the kernel time rose slightly (0.6ms -> 0.7ms) but launch overhead dropped to ~0.9ms and overall tail disappeared in the traces. suggests fallback is the culprit.

sophia: interesting. so selection heuristic is too aggressive for mixed KV workloads. maybe predictor uses average batch size and not the tail distribution.

maya: action items?

oliver: propose: (A) change kernel_selector to consider launch-overhead cost for small-grid variants; (B) add a kvcache sweep backoff when continuous batching is active (defer sweep by 2-4ms baseline); (C) add a perf regression test that runs mixed KV pattern and asserts 95p launch-latency < 3ms.

liam: +1. for A, we can add an extra penalty term P = alpha * estimated_launchs where estimated_launchs = ceil(batch_tokens / grid_size_factor). tune alpha on stage.

perf-bot: created issue INF-1292: "kernel-selector: account for launch overhead in mixed-KV workloads" assigned to @oliver. trace links: https://perfetto.local/trace/2245 and gs://redwood-traces/2245012345/nsys.tar.gz

maya: can you also link the nsys .qdrep snippet? helps perf folks open in Nsight.

oliver: uploaded: gs://redwood-traces/2245012345/nsys.qdrep

sophia: I'll take the sweep backoff patch, small PR with a flag defaulting to off for now.

oliver: thanks. I'll run the forced-grid experiment and post numbers in this thread in ~20m.

liam: ping me if you want to bisect kernel versions — might be a recent change in grid heuristics.

oliver: noted.

(20m later)

oliver: results: forced-grid256 run: 95p latency reduced from 12.1ms -> 6.8ms, launch-wait 95p 4.9ms -> 1.1ms. KV miss injection at 30% still within SLOs. attaching numbers: gs://redwood-metrics/2245012345/summary.csv

maya: awesome. file a small hotfix to kernel_selector with alpha=0.7 and let's roll to stage behind a feature flag. :thumbsup:

oliver: will open PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823

sophia: adding CI perf test as part of the PR would be ideal. I'll draft it and tag you.

liam: great detective work. this pattern likely explains a few unexplained microbursts in the last month.

oliver: thanks team. closing this trace for now, will reopen if regressions reappear. :wave:
